The address is taken after Settings > Network > Trusted proxies applies, so a CDN or load balancer in front does not hide the client. A hostname, such as a dynamic-DNS name, is looked up again when its record expires and matches every address it resolves to: an IPv4 address exactly, an IPv6 address with its /64 (end the name in /56, /128 and so on to change that).

caddyL4.name: Layer 4 Proxy
caddyL4.description: TCP/UDP proxying. Required by L4 proxy hosts and by the agent that binds their ports.

caddyTailscale.name: Tailscale
caddyTailscale.description: Runs Tailscale inside Caddy. Required to serve a proxy host on your tailnet, to gate one on Tailscale identity, and to reach an upstream over the tailnet.

caddyBlocker.name: Request Blocker
caddyBlocker.description: Country, continent, ASN, and CIDR blocking. Required by global geoblocking and by per-host geoblock rules.

cacheHandler.name: HTTP Cache
cacheHandler.description: A shared HTTP cache (Souin) in front of upstreams. Enables the Caddy cache mode of a proxy host's Cache assets option.

souinStorageOtter.name: Otter Cache Storage
souinStorageOtter.description: An in-memory store for the HTTP cache, bounded by entry count and faster than the built-in one. Entries are lost on restart.

souinStorageBadger.name: Badger Cache Storage
souinStorageBadger.description: Keeps the HTTP cache on disk in a Badger database on the Caddy data volume, so it survives a restart.

souinStorageSimplefs.name: SimpleFS Cache Storage
souinStorageSimplefs.description: Keeps the HTTP cache as plain files on the Caddy data volume, so it survives a restart.

souinStorageRedis.name: Redis Cache Storage
souinStorageRedis.description: Keeps the HTTP cache in Redis or Valkey, shared by every Caddy that points at the same server.

souinStorageEtcd.name: etcd Cache Storage
souinStorageEtcd.description: Keeps the HTTP cache in an etcd cluster, shared by every Caddy that points at it. No authentication.

caddyRatelimit.name: Rate Limit
caddyRatelimit.description: Sliding-window request limits per client. Required by a proxy host's Rate limiting option.

caddyCrowdsec.name: CrowdSec
caddyCrowdsec.description: A CrowdSec bouncer: refuses clients your CrowdSec Local API has banned, on proxy hosts and L4 hosts, with optional AppSec. Required by the CrowdSec settings.

corazaWaf.name: Coraza WAF
corazaWaf.description: ModSecurity-compatible web application firewall with the OWASP Core Rule Set. Required by the WAF settings and the WAF events page.

proxyHosts.forwardAuthBypassHeadersHelp: A request carrying any of these headers skips forward auth entirely, and the upstream has to check the credential itself. Comma-separated.
proxyHosts.forwardAuthCopyHeadersHelp: Headers taken from the auth server's answer and set on the request sent upstream. One per line. The same headers are stripped from every inbound request, so they cannot be forged.

proxyHosts.tailscaleUpstreamNodeHelp: Node to dial the upstreams through, for a backend that only exists on your tailnet. Upstream IP pinning and custom DNS resolvers do not apply: MagicDNS resolves names on the far side.
proxyHosts.notesHelp: Anything worth remembering about this host. Only people who can see the host can read them.
proxyHosts.unhealthyLatencyHelp: Latency above which an upstream is marked unhealthy
proxyHosts.wafBodyLimitsDescription: Coraza buffers request bodies for inspection and rejects anything larger than its limit, which is 12.5 MiB with the OWASP CRS loaded. Raise it for hosts that receive large uploads. Leave blank to inherit.
proxyHosts.wafDescription: Inspect and block malicious requests via Coraza / OWASP CRS
proxyHosts.forceHttpsHelp: Redirect plain HTTP requests to HTTPS
proxyHosts.hstsHelp: Tell browsers to only ever use HTTPS for this host. Requires Force HTTPS
proxyHosts.websocketSupportHelp: Allow WebSocket upgrades. The WAF checks the handshake but not the messages after it
proxyHosts.preserveHostHeaderHelp: Send the original Host header to the upstream instead of the upstream's own address
proxyHosts.hstsSubdomainsHelp: Include subdomains in the Strict-Transport-Security header
proxyHosts.skipHttpsValidationHelp: Skip TLS certificate hostname verification for backend connections
proxyHosts.maintenanceDescription: Answer every request with a 503 while the upstream is being worked on. The domain keeps its certificate, and addresses in the bypass list still reach the upstream
proxyHosts.maintenanceActiveDescription: Only the bypass addresses reach the upstream. Access lists, sign-in and the WAF still apply to them
proxyHosts.maintenanceBypassHelp: IP addresses or CIDR ranges, one per line, that skip the maintenance page. Add your own, so you can check the site before reopening it. The client IP honours Settings → Network → Trusted proxies
proxyHosts.maintenanceRetryAfterHelp: Tells clients and crawlers when to come back. Leave it empty to send none
proxyHosts.maintenanceBodyHelp: HTML shown to visitors. Leave it empty to use this host's 503 error page, then the global one, then a built-in page
proxyHosts.anubisDescription: Make browsers solve a proof-of-work challenge from your Anubis instance before they reach the upstream, after geo blocking and the WAF and before any sign-in. Scrapers that cannot run JavaScript never get through
proxyHosts.anubisUpstreamHelp: Where Caddy reaches Anubis, running in subrequest mode (TARGET set to a single space). One instance can serve every host
proxyHosts.anubisExemptPathsHelp: Caddy path patterns, one per line, that skip the challenge. API clients, feeds and webhooks cannot solve one
proxyHosts.rateLimitDescription: Answer clients that send too many requests with 429 Too Many Requests, before geo blocking and the WAF see them.
proxyHosts.rateLimitPathsHelp: Caddy path patterns separated by spaces, such as /login or /api/*. Empty covers every request.
proxyHosts.rateLimitWindowInvalid: Use a number and a unit, such as 10s, 1m or 1h
proxyHosts.rateLimitHeaderInvalid: A header name has no spaces or braces
proxyHosts.rateLimitKeyHeaderHelp: Counts per value of this header, such as an API key. A request without it is counted by its client IP. Clients choose their own header values, so pair it with a per-IP zone if that matters.
proxyHosts.rateLimitKeyUserHelp: Counts per user that forward auth signed in (CPM, Authentik or another forward-auth server that sends Remote-User), checked after sign-in. Requests with no signed-in user, and hosts without forward auth, are counted by client IP.
proxyHosts.rateLimitMethodsHelp: Only these methods count. None selected counts every method.

rateLimitModes.merge: Global zones and this host's own

rateLimitModeHelp.inherit: This host is limited by the zones in Settings > Rate limiting, and has none of its own.
rateLimitModeHelp.merge: The zones in Settings > Rate limiting apply, and so do the ones below. Each keeps its own count.
rateLimitModeHelp.override: Only the zones below apply. Turn it off to have no rate limiting on this host at all.

proxyHosts.rateLimitHelp: Each zone allows a number of requests per client in a sliding window. A request over the limit gets a 429 with Retry-After, rendered by this host's 429 error page when it has one. The client IP honours trusted proxies. An IPv6 prefix such as 64 counts a whole network as one client. Addresses on the never-limited list in Settings > Rate limiting are never counted.
proxyHosts.crowdsecDescription: Refuse clients your CrowdSec Local API has a decision against, before rate limiting, geo blocking and the WAF. Applies once CrowdSec is set up under Settings > CrowdSec.
proxyHosts.upstreamTimeoutsDescription: How long to wait on the upstream before giving up. A field left empty keeps Caddy's default, and location rules use the same values
proxyHosts.upstreamTimeoutInvalid: Use a number and a unit, such as 30s, 1m30s or 2h
proxyHosts.upstreamTimeoutsTailscaleNote: Through a Tailscale node only the two stream settings apply

dialTimeout.label: Connect
dialTimeout.help: Opening a connection, name lookup included. Caddy's default is 3s

responseHeaderTimeout.label: Response headers
responseHeaderTimeout.help: From sending the request to receiving the response headers. No limit by default

readTimeout.label: Read
readTimeout.help: The longest wait for the next read from the upstream. No limit by default

writeTimeout.label: Write
writeTimeout.help: The longest wait for a write to the upstream. No limit by default

keepAliveIdleTimeout.label: Idle connection
keepAliveIdleTimeout.help: How long an unused connection is kept open for reuse. Caddy's default is 2m

streamTimeout.label: Stream lifetime
streamTimeout.help: Closes WebSockets and other upgraded connections after this long. No limit by default

streamCloseDelay.label: Stream close delay
streamCloseDelay.help: How long upgraded connections survive a config reload. Closed at once by default

proxyHosts.skipAccessLog: Leave out of the access log
proxyHosts.skipAccessLogHelp: Caddy writes no access-log line for this host, so it does not appear in the log viewer or analytics. Useful for a dashboard or health-check host that would otherwise fill the log
proxyHosts.discourageIndexingHelp: Ask search engines not to index this host: every response gets X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow, and /robots.txt disallows everything, even behind a sign-in. Well-behaved crawlers honour it; it doesn't keep anyone out
proxyHosts.compressionHelp: Compress text responses with zstd or gzip. Default follows Settings → Network → Compression
proxyHosts.proxyHostActiveDescription: This host is active and routing traffic
proxyHosts.proxyHostPausedDescription: This host is disabled and does not respond to requests
proxyHosts.atLeastOneUpstreamRequired: At least one upstream is required

geoipStatus.offHelp: GeoIP is switched off in Settings → Geo-blocking → GeoIP databases, so country, continent and ASN blocking does not work.
geoipStatus.missingHelp: GeoIP databases not found, so country, continent and ASN blocking does not work. Add a MaxMind subscription under Settings → Geo-blocking → GeoIP databases.
geoipStatus.countryMissingHelp: GeoLite2-Country database missing, so country and continent blocking is off
geoipStatus.asnMissingHelp: GeoLite2-ASN database missing, so ASN blocking is off

proxyHosts.asnsHelp: Autonomous System Numbers. Press Enter to add each one
proxyHosts.trustedProxiesHelp: Used to parse X-Forwarded-For. Use private_ranges for all RFC-1918 ranges.
proxyHosts.upstreamDialledThrough: Upstreams are dialled through {node}. Use a MagicDNS name or a tailnet IP in the Upstreams field above.
proxyHosts.dnsPinningSummaryInherit: Using global upstream DNS pinning defaults
proxyHosts.dnsPinningSummaryOverride: Override: {mode, select, inherit {inherit mode} enabled {enabled} disabled {disabled} other {{mode}}}, {family, select, inherit {inherit family} both {both} ipv6 {IPv6} ipv4 {IPv4} other {{family}}}
proxyHosts.hostCreated: Proxy host created and queued for Caddy reload.
proxyHosts.hostCreatedAutoCert: Proxy host created. Certificate ID {id} was not found, so the host uses 'Managed by Caddy (Auto)', which provisions certificates through Caddy.
proxyHosts.hostCreatedAutoCertNoCloudflare: Proxy host created. Certificate ID {id} was not found, so the host uses 'Managed by Caddy (Auto)'. Without Cloudflare DNS integration, wildcard certificates need port 80 reachable for HTTP-01 challenges. Configure Cloudflare in Settings to use DNS-01 challenges.
proxyHosts.hostUpdatedAutoCert: Proxy host updated. Certificate ID {id} was not found, so the host uses 'Managed by Caddy (Auto)', which provisions certificates through Caddy.
proxyHosts.hostUpdatedAutoCertNoCloudflare: Proxy host updated. Certificate ID {id} was not found, so the host uses 'Managed by Caddy (Auto)'. Without Cloudflare DNS integration, wildcard certificates need port 80 reachable for HTTP-01 challenges. Configure Cloudflare in Settings to use DNS-01 challenges.
proxyHosts.maintenanceOnResult: Maintenance mode is on: visitors get a 503.
proxyHosts.wafPresetsHelpMerge: Added to the presets the global WAF settings select.
proxyHosts.wafPresetsHelpOverride: Only these presets apply. Override mode ignores the global selection.
proxyHosts.wafPluginsHelpMerge: Added to the plugins the global WAF settings select. Plugins load only with the OWASP CRS.
proxyHosts.wafPluginsHelpOverride: Only these plugins apply. Override mode ignores the global selection. Plugins load only with the OWASP CRS.
proxyHosts.wafExclusionsMoved: Rule exclusions for this host, scoped to a path or a variable if you like, are managed on the WAF page.
proxyHosts.wafLegacyExclusions: Still excluded from an older version, until the next restart moves them to the WAF page:

auditStreaming.help: Every audit event goes to each enabled sink in order, at least once, with its seq, hash and prevHash so the receiver can check that nothing is missing or out of order. A new sink starts from the oldest event the log still holds.
auditStreaming.emptyDescription: Add a sink to send the audit log to a syslog server, an HTTP receiver or a file.
auditStreaming.saveFailed: The sink could not be saved.
auditStreaming.deleteFailed: The sink could not be deleted.
auditStreaming.deleteConfirm: {name} stops receiving the audit log. What it already received stays with the receiver.

kindHelp.syslogUdp: RFC 5424 messages, one per datagram. Nothing confirms delivery, so prefer TCP or TLS where the server offers it.
kindHelp.syslogTcp: RFC 5424 messages with octet-counting framing. Unencrypted: use it only on a network you trust.
kindHelp.syslogTls: RFC 5424 messages with octet-counting framing over TLS. Nothing is sent until the server's certificate checks out for the hostname.
kindHelp.http: Batches of records POSTed as newline-delimited JSON.
kindHelp.file: Appended to a file on the data volume, one JSON record per line, for a local shipper to pick up.

auditStreaming.lagAudit: {count, plural, one {# audit event} other {# audit events}}
auditStreaming.lagSecurity: {count, plural, one {# security record} other {# security records}}
auditStreaming.maxBytesHelp: {min} to {max}. A longer record keeps its header and its seq, hash and prevHash whole; the JSON after them is cut and the message marked truncated.
auditStreaming.caHelp: A PEM certificate to trust for this sink, besides the system's authorities. For a receiver with a certificate from a private CA.
auditStreaming.urlHelp: Plain http is allowed only to an address on this network.
auditStreaming.encodingHelp: HTTP cannot negotiate the encoding of a request body, so pick what the receiver accepts. If it answers 415, batches go uncompressed and this page says so.
auditStreaming.headerValueHelp: Sent with every batch, for example Bearer and a token. Stored encrypted and never shown again.
auditStreaming.fileNameHelp: Created under audit-stream/ on the data volume.
auditStreaming.includeSecurityHelp: WAF events and other mitigated requests, as records of kind security with a seq of their own, redacted as stored. They are not part of the hash chain and say so. Needs analytics.
auditStreaming.testEncodingRefused: The receiver refused the configured compression, so it went uncompressed. Saved sinks fall back the same way.
auditStreaming.testFailed: The test record did not get through
auditStreaming.gapAudit: Audit events {from} to {to} were pruned before it received them. {missed, plural, one {# record} other {# records}} missed in all; the receiver was sent a gap record in their place.
auditStreaming.gapSecurity: Security records {from} to {to} were dropped before it received them. {missed, plural, one {# record} other {# records}} missed in all; the receiver was sent a gap record in their place.
auditStreaming.encodingFallback: The receiver answered 415 to {encoding}, so batches go uncompressed until the sink is saved again.

backup.title: Backup and restore
backup.downloadHelp: Everything this instance is configured with: hosts, certificates and their keys, access lists, users, groups, API tokens and every setting. Secrets are decrypted into the file and the whole file is encrypted with the passphrase, so it restores onto a new machine with a different SESSION_SECRET.
backup.passphraseHelp: At least {min} characters. It is the only thing protecting the file, and nobody can recover a backup without it.
backup.includeSettingsHistory: Include the settings and host history
backup.notIncluded: Not included: who is signed in, the certificates Caddy has issued (they are issued again), analytics, and the GeoIP databases (they are downloaded again).
backup.downloadFailed: The backup could not be made
backup.restoreHelp: Replaces this instance's whole configuration with the backup's. What is here now is saved to a backup of its own on the controller's data volume first, with the same passphrase. Everyone is signed out afterwards.
backup.keepAgentsHelp: Leave on when restoring onto the same machine. Turn off when moving to a new one: its agents pair again, and hosts assigned to the old agents serve on every agent.
backup.newerHelp: Upgrade this instance first. An older version would silently drop what it doesn't understand.
backup.remoteEmpty: This destination holds no backups yet.
backup.listFailed: Could not list the destination's backups
backup.confirmHelp: Every host, user and setting here is replaced by the backup's. Caddy's certificates are issued again, which can hit your certificate authority's rate limits if there are many hosts.

backupSchedules.destinationsHelp: Where scheduled backups are written: a bucket on any S3-compatible service, or a folder on the controller's data volume.
backupSchedules.destinationsEmptyDescription: Add a bucket or a local folder for scheduled backups to go to.
backupSchedules.endpointHelp: The service's S3 URL. Leave empty for Amazon S3 itself, where the region picks the address.
backupSchedules.secretStored: A secret is stored. Leave empty to keep it, unless the endpoint, bucket or key ID changes.
backupSchedules.virtualHostedStyleHelp: Address the bucket as bucket.endpoint rather than endpoint/bucket. Some providers require one or the other.
backupSchedules.folderHelp: Under backups/ on the controller's data volume. Copy it somewhere else as well: a backup on the same disk does not survive losing that disk.
backupSchedules.prefixHelp: Prepended to every file name, for sharing a bucket with other data.
backupSchedules.testPassed: The destination works: a test file was written, read back and deleted
backupSchedules.deleteDestinationConfirm: {name} is removed from this list. Backups already written there stay where they are.
backupSchedules.schedulesHelp: Each schedule makes a sealed backup on its own timing and writes it to a destination. One controller runs them; if it was down when one was due, the next controller to take over runs the latest it missed.
backupSchedules.schedulesEmptyDescription: Add a schedule to back up this instance automatically.
backupSchedules.schedulesNeedDestination: Add a destination first: a schedule needs somewhere to write.
backupSchedules.expressionHelp: Five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week. For example 0 */6 * * * runs every six hours.
backupSchedules.timeZoneHelp: An IANA name such as Europe/Berlin. The schedule follows its daylight-saving changes.
backupSchedules.schedulePrefixHelp: Added after the destination's prefix. Old backups are pruned only from directly under this prefix, and only files this schedule names.
backupSchedules.retentionHelp: A backup is deleted once neither rule keeps it. Leave both empty to keep every backup.
backupSchedules.passphraseKeep: Leave empty to keep the stored passphrase. Backups already made keep the passphrase they were made with.
backupSchedules.passphraseStoredTitle: The passphrase is stored on this instance
backupSchedules.passphraseStored: Scheduled runs need nobody present, so the passphrase is kept, encrypted with SESSION_SECRET. Anyone who has that secret can already read this database, so this exposes nothing new, but keep a copy of the passphrase elsewhere: without it no backup can be restored.
backupSchedules.runningHelp: This takes a few seconds, longer with the audit log included.
backupSchedules.deleteScheduleConfirm: {name} stops running. Backups it already wrote stay at the destination.

configTransfer.heading: Portable configuration
configTransfer.intro: Move hosts and the configuration around them to another instance, or keep it under version control. Unlike a backup it merges: nothing on the receiving side is removed, and users, API tokens, sessions, agents and the audit log stay where they are.
configTransfer.exportHelp: A JSON file you can read and review. Secrets in it (certificate keys, passwords, API tokens, credentials inside host settings) are each sealed with the passphrase.

sections.hosts: Proxy hosts and L4 hosts, with their agent pins, mTLS rules and sign-in grants
sections.accessLists: Access lists, their users and their rules
sections.certificates: Certificates (imported ones with their keys), CAs, client certificates and mTLS roles
sections.groups: Groups, their members, IdP mappings and grants
sections.security: WAF presets, CRS plugins, WAF exclusions and blocked sources

configTransfer.importHelp: Rows are matched by name (hosts, lists, certificates, groups), users by email and agents by their agent ID, or by name when only one agent has it. A name more than one row shares is skipped. You see exactly what would change before anything does.
configTransfer.unchangedHidden: {count, plural, one {# row is already identical here and is not listed.} other {# rows are already identical here and are not listed.}}

reasons.domainConflict: {domain} is already served by {host}, which is left as it is
reasons.listenerConflict: {listen} is already used by {host}, which is left as it is
reasons.missingReference: Names {name} ({kind}), which this instance does not have
reasons.unkeyable: Has no name to match it by
reasons.ambiguous: More than one row is called {name}, here or in the file, so none of them is matched

warnings.rowDropped: {parent}: an entry naming {missingName} ({missingKind}) is left out, since this instance does not have it

configTransfer.nothingToDo: Everything in the file is already here. Nothing would change.
configTransfer.confirmHelp: The rows listed are created or updated and Caddy is reloaded. Nothing else here changes.

settings.abortResponseDescription: Caddy writes no status line or body, the same as a "444 / no response" policy.
settings.abortResponseTitle: Unmatched connections are closed without a response
settings.accessLogsCommand: View with: docker exec caddy-proxy-manager-caddy tail -f /logs/access.log
settings.accessLogsInfoTitle: Access logs live in the caddy-logs Docker volume
settings.acmeDirectoryHelp: Leave empty to use the Let's Encrypt default. For an internal CA (OpenBao, Step-CA, Windows ADCS), paste its ACME directory URL. It must be HTTPS.
settings.acmeEmailHelp: Used by Let's Encrypt for expiry notifications.
settings.acmeRootCertificateHelp: If the ACME endpoint's TLS certificate is signed by an internal root not in the system trust store, paste the root (or chain) here so Caddy can connect to it.
settings.agentManagementUnavailableTitle: No agent is answering, so the container cannot be managed from here
settings.agentsDescription: An agent recreates, rebuilds and configures the Caddy container on its host. The controller has no Docker access of its own, and no address for any Caddy: everything reaches a proxy through its agent.
settings.autoPairingDisabledDescription: Unpairing the bundled agent turned auto-pairing off, so it stays idle instead of pairing itself straight back. Turn it on again to let it pair within a few seconds.
settings.passkeyHostnameWarningTitle: Passkeys are tied to this hostname
settings.passkeyHostnameWarningDescription: Every passkey registered here belongs to {host}. Change the Public URL to another hostname and none of them will sign in again: people use their password or single sign-on, then add a new passkey.
settings.autoPairingDisabledTitle: The bundled agent will not pair itself
settings.enableAutoPairing: Let the bundled agent pair itself
settings.repairBootstrapIssued: This is the bundled agent, so a token for it was left on the data volume. If it is idle it pairs itself within a few seconds. The token expires in 30 minutes.
settings.repairCodeHelp: Only this agent can use this code, and it replaces the agent's current secret. Valid for five minutes. Run this on that agent's host:
settings.analyticsCollectionHelp: Record every proxied request and every WAF event, and show them on the Analytics page. With this off, no events are written and the agents stop reading Caddy's logs.
settings.analyticsRetentionHelp: How long events are kept. Lowering it migrates the existing tables' TTL, which rewrites their parts.
settings.authentikDefaultsHelp: Host-level settings can override this default
settings.backChannelLogoutHelp: Optional. Set this as the provider's back-channel logout URL and CPM will end a user's sessions when the identity provider ends theirs.
settings.clientIpHeadersHelp: Headers Caddy reads the client IP from, one per line. Empty defaults to X-Forwarded-For. For Cloudflare, set Cf-Connecting-Ip.
settings.dashboardCheckNeedsSaveDescription: The check asks the domain that is saved, not the one in the field. Save first, then check.
settings.dashboardCheckNeedsSaveTitle: Save the domain before checking it
settings.dashboardDisableConfirmBody: You are reading this page on {domain}, which is the domain about to stop being served. Saving takes this route away while you are using it.
settings.dashboardDisableConfirmRecovery: The dashboard stays reachable on the controller's own port, http://'<host>':3000, where you can turn this back on.
settings.dashboardDnsMatchDescription: A request sent to that domain came back to this instance, signed. DNS, the network in between, and Caddy's route all work, so HTTPS has been switched on.
settings.dashboardDnsMismatchDescription: The domain resolves to {resolved}, but a request sent to it did not arrive here: it reached a different server, or nothing answered on port 80. HTTPS has been switched off; a certificate order would fail the same way.
settings.dashboardDnsMismatchTitle: The domain does not reach this instance
settings.dashboardDnsUnresolvedDescription: Nothing answers for that name yet. Create an A or AAAA record pointing at this deployment, then check again.
settings.dashboardDomainHelp: The name this dashboard answers on, once it is served through Caddy.
settings.dashboardEnabledHelp: Serves this dashboard through the Caddy this instance manages, as a host it maintains for you.
settings.dashboardProxyOptionsHelp: Everything a proxy host can be configured with, applied to this dashboard's route: certificate, access list, agents, headers, WAF, geo-blocking and the rest. The upstream is always this controller. CPM forward auth and mTLS access rules are not offered here, because they are stored against a proxy host.
settings.dashboardPortEscapeDescription: This host is generated from the settings above rather than stored in Proxy hosts, so nothing can delete it by accident. The controller also publishes its own port, so http://'<host>':3000 reaches this page whatever happens to the route.
settings.dashboardPortEscapeTitle: You cannot lock yourself out with this
settings.dashboardTlsHelp: Forces HTTPS and asks Caddy for a certificate. Only useful once requests to the domain arrive here.
settings.dashboardTlsUnverifiedDescription: The last check did not confirm that this domain reaches here. Caddy keeps retrying the certificate order, and the domain does not serve over HTTPS until it succeeds.
settings.dashboardTlsUnverifiedTitle: HTTPS is on, but reachability was not confirmed
settings.defaultDomainHelp: Filled in for you when you create a proxy host, so the domain you use most is already there.
settings.defaultGeoblockTrustedProxies: Default geoblock trusted proxies from this list
settings.defaultRedirectStatusHelp: 307 and 308 preserve the original request method.
settings.defaultRedirectUrlHelp: Targets can be absolute, relative or built from Caddy placeholders.
settings.defaultResponseBehaviorHelp: Applied only when no configured proxy host matches the request.
settings.defaultResponseBodyHelp: Plain text, JSON, or custom HTML. Empty is allowed.
settings.defaultResponseHeadersHelp: Optional Name: value pairs, one per line. For custom HTML, set Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8.
settings.defaultResponsePriorityTitle: Configured hosts always run before this catch-all
settings.defaultResponseStatusHelp: Any final HTTP status from 200 through 599.
settings.defaultResponseTlsDescription: For HTTPS the response can only be sent once a TLS certificate completes the handshake, so an unknown hostname or direct IP may fail earlier.
settings.dnsAddressFamilyHelp: Both resolves AAAA and A records and orders IPv6 addresses first.
settings.dnsPinningHelp: Resolves upstream hostnames at config-apply time and writes IPs into Caddy's active config.
settings.dnsPinningInfoDescription: Resolution happens at config save/reload time, and resolved IPs are written into Caddy's active config. If one handler has multiple different HTTPS upstream hostnames, HTTPS pinning is skipped for those HTTPS upstreams to avoid SNI mismatch.
settings.dnsProviderModuleDisabledDescription: Enable it under Settings → Caddy build and rebuild Caddy before using it for DNS-01 challenges. Credentials saved now are not used until then.
settings.dnsProviderModuleDisabledTitle: This provider's Caddy module is disabled
settings.dnsResolversInfoDescription: For a DNS provider with slow propagation, or for split-horizon DNS. Common public resolvers: 1.1.1.1 (Cloudflare), 194.242.2.2 (Mullvad), 9.9.9.9 (Quad9).
settings.environmentOverrideTitle: Currently set by an environment variable
settings.ephemeralNodesHelp: Ephemeral nodes disappear from the tailnet when Caddy stops, instead of lingering as offline machines. Their identity is not reused, so a restart shows up as a new device.
settings.accentColorPinned: Set by {env}, which overrides what is stored here.
settings.faviconUploadHelp: PNG, ICO, SVG, WebP, GIF or JPEG, up to 256 KB. A square image of at least 32×32 works everywhere; browsers scale it down themselves.
settings.faviconTooltipReplace: Replace the favicon with another image
settings.faviconWillBeRemoved: The custom favicon is removed when you save.
settings.geoblockTrustedProxiesHelp: Use these ranges as the default trusted-proxy list for global geoblocking so the two can't silently disagree. A geoblock list set explicitly wins.
settings.geoipBehind: MaxMind has a newer {editions} than the copy on disk, and it has not been downloaded yet.
settings.geoipDownloadsDescription: It checks MaxMind on the interval below using these credentials. Agents fetch the databases from this controller rather than each holding a licence key.
settings.geoipDownloadsTitle: This controller downloads the databases itself
settings.geoipHelp: Country lookups for analytics, and the country matching that geo blocking is built on. With this off, the geo block fields are marked as off and events record no country.
settings.geoipNeverChecked: MaxMind has never been checked for updates.
settings.geoipSavedDisabled: GeoIP disabled. Country matching is no longer offered.
settings.geoipSavedEnabled: GeoIP enabled. Downloading the databases from MaxMind.
settings.geoipSavedNeedsCredentials: GeoIP enabled. Add a MaxMind account ID and licence key to download the databases.
settings.geoipUpdateDisabled: Turn GeoIP on and save to download the databases.
settings.geoipUpdateIntervalHelp: MaxMind rebuilds GeoLite2 ASN daily, and Country and City on Tuesdays and Fridays. A check downloads only what changed.
settings.geoipUpdateUnconfigured: Add a MaxMind account ID and licence key to download the databases.
settings.globalErrorPagesHelp: These error pages apply to every proxy host as a fallback. A per-host error page for the same status code takes precedence.
settings.gravatarEnvironmentOverrideTitle: Gravatar is set by the AVATAR_GRAVATAR environment variable
settings.gravatarHelp: For users with no icon of their own, look one up from gravatar.com by their email address. Their browser contacts gravatar.com directly, which discloses their IP and a hash of their address to a third party. Accounts with a local-only address are never looked up, and anyone without a Gravatar falls back to their initial.
settings.gravatarLabel: Use Gravatar when a user has no icon
settings.groupMappingHelp: Derive CPM roles and groups from the identity provider's group claim.
settings.groupPrefixHelp: Shorthand for naming the role groups: with prefix CPM_, members of CPM_Admin become admins, CPM_User users and CPM_Viewer viewers. Name the groups below instead if they do not share a prefix.
settings.groupSyncHelp: Creates CPM groups from the remaining prefixed claims (with the prefix stripped) for forward-auth access control. Groups you created yourself are never modified.
settings.rolesClaimHelp: Claim holding the roles that decide a user's role here, when your provider keeps them apart from groups (Keycloak's realm_access.roles, Entra's roles). Empty reads them from the groups claim above. The names below match against it.
settings.groupsClaimHelp: Claim holding the user's groups. Use dots for nested claims, e.g. resource_access.cpm.roles. Remember to request a matching scope above.
settings.homeAttentionCount: {count, plural, one {# setting is} other {# settings are}} configured but not working as intended
settings.imageRepositoryHelp: Where this deployment's images come from, without the image name. Point it at your own namespace if you run a fork, otherwise it reports releases you cannot pull.
settings.issuerUrlHelp: For OIDC providers, the issuer URL lets CPM discover the endpoints automatically.
settings.legacyPasswordResetHelp: New passwords are hashed with argon2id. Accounts created before that change still use bcrypt, which caps the password at 72 bytes. Turning this on sends those users to a reset screen at their next sign-in; choosing a new password upgrades the hash and clears the prompt. Users who sign in through an OAuth/OIDC provider have no password and are never asked.
settings.legacyPasswordResetLabel: Require a password change for users still on an older hash
settings.localAgentDescription: It is reached over a socket on the shared data volume and needs no pairing. Pair a remote agent below only if Caddy runs on a different host from this controller.
settings.managedAnalyticsTitle: The agent starts and stops ClickHouse for you
settings.maxmindCredentialsHelp: From your MaxMind account. Without a subscription the databases cannot be downloaded, though GeoIP still works if you supply the files another way.
settings.metricsEndpointHelp: Prometheus-compatible scrape endpoint, exposed on a dedicated port.
settings.metricsInfoTitle: Point your monitoring tool at the metrics endpoint
settings.metricsPortHelp: Separate from the admin API on port 2019.
settings.oauthAutoLinkHelp: Signing in through this provider attaches to the existing user with the same email address. When off, users link it themselves from their profile.
settings.forwardAuthSequentialIdsTitle: Forward auth still sends numeric user IDs
settings.forwardAuthSequentialIdsDescription: Applications behind forward auth receive each account's sequential number as X-CPM-User-Id, which reveals how many accounts exist. Once none of them keys its accounts on that number, turn off {setting} below to send a UUID instead.
settings.forwardAuthSequentialIdsDismiss: Dismiss the numeric user ID notice
settings.pairingCodeExpires: {minutes, plural, one {Valid for # more minute.} other {Valid for # more minutes.}}
settings.pairingCodeFailed: Could not generate a pairing code.
settings.pairingCodeHelp: Generate a code here, then run the pair command on the agent's host. The code is valid for five minutes and works once.
settings.pairingCodeRun: Run this on the agent's host, then confirm the controller name it shows:
settings.passwordPolicyEnvironmentOverrideTitle: This policy is set by the AUTH_REQUIRE_PASSWORD_CHANGE_ON_LEGACY_HASH environment variable
settings.providersEmptyDescription: Add a provider to enable single sign-on.

account_lock_base_delay_ms.description: How long the first lock lasts. Each failure after it doubles the wait.
account_lock_base_delay_ms.label: First account lock (milliseconds)

account_lock_disable_after.description: Counted like the lock above: forgotten a day after the last failure, and reset by a successful sign-in.
account_lock_disable_after.label: Failed sign-ins before an account is disabled

access_review_confirm_revocations.description: A closed access review holds its revocations until an administrator confirms them, instead of applying them as it closes.
access_review_confirm_revocations.label: Revocations wait for confirmation

access_review_reminder_days.description: How many days before an access review's due date its undecided items are reported, through the access review notifications.
access_review_reminder_days.label: Access review reminder (days before due)

account_lock_disable_enabled.description: Disable an account once it reaches the number of failed sign-ins below, until an administrator enables it again. Anyone who knows a username can then disable that account by guessing at it. The last active administrator is never disabled, only locked.
account_lock_disable_enabled.label: Disable accounts after repeated failed sign-ins

account_lock_enabled.description: Slow down guesses at one account whatever address they come from. Separate from the per-client lockout above.
account_lock_enabled.label: Lock accounts after failed sign-ins

account_lock_free_failures.description: How many failures an account takes before each further one locks it.
account_lock_free_failures.label: Failed sign-ins before an account is locked

account_lock_max_delay_ms.description: The doubling stops here, so guessing can slow the owner's sign-in but never shut it off.
account_lock_max_delay_ms.label: Longest account lock (milliseconds)

analytics_enabled.description: Collect traffic and WAF events. With an agent running the stack, turning this on also starts the ClickHouse container, without a Compose profile. If left unset, analytics is on only when a password is configured below.
analytics_enabled.label: Enable analytics

accent_color.description: The colour of selected items, primary buttons and focus rings across the dashboard.
accent_color.label: Accent colour

app_name.description: Shown in the sidebar, on the login card, and as the suffix on every page title.
app_name.label: Application name

auth_allow_oauth_registration.description: Let a first-time OAuth identity create an account. Separate from self-registration: with this off, existing users can still sign in and link.
auth_allow_oauth_registration.label: Allow OAuth registration

auth_allow_oauth_role_from_claims.description: Let the provider's claims set a new user's role and status. With this off they are forced to user/active regardless of what the IdP sends. Only enable it for an IdP you control.
auth_allow_oauth_role_from_claims.label: Trust IdP role claims

auth_allow_self_registration.description: Let anyone create an account with an email address and password.
auth_allow_self_registration.label: Allow self-registration

auth_disable_local_users.description: Remove local accounts entirely: no credential sign-in, no password management, no bootstrap admin. Turn it on only after confirming that OAuth sign-in works.
auth_disable_local_users.label: OIDC-only mode

auth_rate_limit_enabled.description: Throttle requests to the auth endpoints. Separate from the login throttle below.
auth_rate_limit_enabled.label: Rate-limit auth requests

auth_rate_limit_max.description: How many auth requests one client may make before being throttled.
auth_rate_limit_max.label: Auth requests per window

auth_rate_limit_window.description: The period over which auth requests are counted.
auth_rate_limit_window.label: Auth rate-limit window (seconds)

auth_passkey_autofill.description: Start a passkey sign-in as soon as the sign-in screen opens, offered in the username field's autofill. Off, a passkey is used only when someone clicks Sign in with a passkey.
auth_passkey_autofill.label: Offer passkeys automatically

auth_require_password_change_on_legacy_h.description: Require anyone still on a pre-argon2id bcrypt hash to change their password. Leave unset to let the Security toggle decide.
auth_require_password_change_on_legacy_h.label: Force a reset for legacy password hashes

auth_trust_host.description: Build URLs from the request's Host header. Use it only behind a proxy that rewrites it, and only when the public URL above cannot cover the setup.
auth_trust_host.label: Trust the Host header

avatar_gravatar.description: Let user icons fall back to gravatar.com, which the browser fetches directly. Turn off to keep every avatar lookup off the network.
avatar_gravatar.label: Gravatar fallback

base_url.description: The address users reach this instance at. OAuth redirect URIs are built from it, so it must match what the provider has registered.
base_url.label: Public URL

caddy_api_url.description: Where Caddy's admin API is reachable, for a deployment running Caddy with no agent. With an agent, every admin call is proxied through it and this is not used.
caddy_api_url.label: Caddy admin API

caddy_monitor_enabled.label: Re-apply after a Caddy restart
caddy_monitor_enabled.description: Watch every Caddy for a restart onto a config this controller did not send, and push its configuration back. Turn it off only on a controller sharing a Caddy it does not own; otherwise the two keep pushing their own config over each other's.

caddy_build_timeout.description: How long to wait for an xcaddy rebuild before giving up. Caddy compiles from source, so slow or ARM hosts can take much longer than the default.
caddy_build_timeout.label: Caddy build timeout (seconds)

clickhouse_db.description: The database traffic and WAF events are written to.
clickhouse_db.label: ClickHouse database

clickhouse_password.description: Required for analytics: the ClickHouse container refuses to start without one, and with it empty there is nothing to authenticate as.
clickhouse_password.label: ClickHouse password

host_history_keep_revisions.description: Each host keeps at least this many of its latest revisions, however old. Older ones are removed once they are also past the age below.
host_history_keep_revisions.label: Host revisions kept

host_history_keep_days.description: Revisions younger than this are kept, however many a host has. A deleted host keeps its history too, so it can be restored.
host_history_keep_days.label: Host history kept (days)

audit_log_keep_days.description: Audit events older than this are removed once a day, and the removal is itself recorded. 0 keeps them forever.
audit_log_keep_days.label: Audit log kept (days)

clickhouse_retention_days.description: How long traffic and WAF events are kept. Lowering it uses less disk, and migrates the existing tables' TTL on the next start.
clickhouse_retention_days.label: Analytics retention (days)

clickhouse_url.description: Where the analytics database is reachable.
clickhouse_url.label: ClickHouse URL

clickhouse_user.description: The account traffic and WAF events are written as.
clickhouse_user.label: ClickHouse user

forward_auth_allowed_ports.description: Non-default ports that CPM forward-auth sites are served on, comma-separated. Caddy matches a host whatever the port, so a sign-in on a port that is neither listed here nor the default for http or https is refused.
forward_auth_allowed_ports.label: Forward-auth ports

forward_auth_sequential_user_ids.description: Send X-CPM-User-Id as the sequential account number instead of a UUID. Sequential ids reveal how many accounts exist. Changing this changes the id every upstream sees for every user.
forward_auth_sequential_user_ids.label: Numeric forward-auth user IDs

forward_auth_internal_url.description: The address Caddy uses to reach this app for forward_auth. When empty, it is derived from the container network. Set it only if that address is wrong.
forward_auth_internal_url.label: Internal forward-auth address

geoip_enabled.description: Country lookups for analytics and geo blocking. If a MaxMind account ID and licence key are set, turning this on also makes the controller download the databases. If left unset, GeoIP is on only when the databases are already present.
geoip_enabled.label: Enable GeoIP

geoip_update_interval_hours.description: How often the controller asks MaxMind for newer databases. MaxMind rebuilds GeoLite2 ASN daily, and Country and City on Tuesdays and Fridays. A check downloads only what changed.
geoip_update_interval_hours.label: Update check interval (hours)

geoipupdate_account_id.description: Needed to download GeoLite2 databases, which geo blocking depends on.
geoipupdate_account_id.label: MaxMind account ID

geoipupdate_license_key.description: Issued alongside the account ID at maxmind.com.
geoipupdate_license_key.label: MaxMind licence key

login_block_ms.description: How long a blocked client stays blocked.
login_block_ms.label: Lockout duration (milliseconds)

login_max_attempts.description: How many failed sign-ins one client may make before it is blocked.
login_max_attempts.label: Failed logins before lockout

login_window_ms.description: The period over which failed sign-ins are counted.
login_window_ms.label: Sign-in window (milliseconds)

update_check_enabled.description: Check the registry below a few times a day for a newer release.
update_check_enabled.label: Check for updates

update_check_prereleases.description: Also watch for betas and release candidates, and show a notice here when one is newer than what's running. Stable installs still only receive stable releases.
update_check_prereleases.label: Check for prereleases

update_image_repository.description: Where this deployment's images come from, without the image name. The update check reads its tags. Point it at your own namespace if you run a fork, otherwise it reports releases you cannot pull.
update_image_repository.label: Image repository

smtp_enabled.description: Password reset links, invitations and certificate alerts go out through the SMTP server below. If left unset, email is on whenever a server is named.
smtp_enabled.label: Send email

smtp_host.description: The hostname or address of the mail server to relay through.
smtp_host.label: SMTP server

smtp_port.description: Usually 587 for STARTTLS, 465 for implicit TLS and 25 for an unencrypted relay.
smtp_port.label: SMTP port

smtp_security.description: starttls upgrades the connection and refuses a server that cannot; tls encrypts from the first byte; none sends in the clear, for a relay on a trusted network only.
smtp_security.label: SMTP encryption

smtp_username.description: Leave empty for a relay that accepts mail without signing in.
smtp_username.label: SMTP username

smtp_password.description: Sent only after the connection is encrypted, unless encryption is set to none.
smtp_password.label: SMTP password

smtp_from.description: The From address on every message. Many servers refuse one the account is not allowed to send as.
smtp_from.label: Sender address

smtp_from_name.description: The name shown beside the sender address. If left empty, the application name is used.
smtp_from_name.label: Sender name

email_alert_recipients.description: Comma-separated addresses for certificate alerts, and extra recipients of every notification. If left empty, certificate alerts go to every active administrator.
email_alert_recipients.label: Alert recipients

certificate_expiry_alert_days.description: Email the alert recipients once a certificate has fewer days than this left. Caddy renews on its own well before then, so an alert means renewal is failing. 0 turns alerts off.
certificate_expiry_alert_days.label: Certificate alert threshold (days)

notify_account_disabled.description: When an account is disabled after failed sign-ins, or the last administrator is kept enabled.
notify_account_disabled.label: Account disabled after failed sign-ins

notify_admin_locked.description: When failed sign-ins lock an administrator's account.
notify_admin_locked.label: Administrator account locked

notify_admin_added.description: When an administrator account is created, or a user is made an administrator.
notify_admin_added.label: New administrator

notify_agent_offline.description: When an agent stays disconnected longer than the time below, and when it is back.
notify_agent_offline.label: Agent offline

notify_agent_offline_minutes.description: How long an agent may be disconnected before anyone is notified. After a restart of this server every agent gets this long to reconnect.
notify_agent_offline_minutes.label: Agent offline after (minutes)

notify_upstream_errors.description: When a proxy host answers 502, 503 or 504 as often as set below, and when it has been quiet for as long again. Read from the access log, so access logging must be on.
notify_upstream_errors.label: Upstream errors

notify_upstream_error_count.description: How many 502, 503 or 504 responses from one host, within the minutes below.
notify_upstream_error_count.label: Upstream errors before notifying (responses)

notify_upstream_error_minutes.description: Also how long a host must go without one before it counts as recovered.
notify_upstream_error_minutes.label: Upstream error window (minutes)

notify_caddy_apply.description: When Caddy refuses a configuration, and when it loads one again. The agent reports an unreachable Caddy.
notify_caddy_apply.label: Caddy configuration refused

notify_agent_problems.description: When an agent reports a failed Caddy build, optional service or L4 port change, or log files it cannot read or prune.
notify_agent_problems.label: Agent failures

notify_geoip_failed.description: When the GeoIP database update has failed three times in a row, and when it works again.
notify_geoip_failed.label: GeoIP update failing

notify_crs_plugin_disabled.description: When a CRS plugin that Caddy refuses is switched off so the rest of the configuration loads.
notify_crs_plugin_disabled.label: CRS plugin switched off

notify_update_available.description: Once per release, while the update check under General is on.
notify_update_available.label: New release

notify_backup_failed.description: When a scheduled backup fails, and when the schedule's next run works again.
notify_backup_failed.label: Scheduled backup failing

notify_audit_sink_failed.description: When an audit sink keeps failing or falls behind, and when it catches up again.
notify_audit_sink_failed.label: Audit streaming failing

notify_access_reviews.description: When an access review nears its due date or passes it with items undecided, and when one closes with revocations waiting for confirmation.
notify_access_reviews.label: Access reviews

notify_change_approvals.description: When an administrator applies a change request without waiting for its approvals.
notify_change_approvals.label: Change approval bypassed

notify_channel_failing.description: When sends to an alert channel keep failing, reported through the other channels, and when it works again.
notify_channel_failing.label: Alert channel failing

notify_disabled_account_owner.description: Email one message to an account's own address when it is disabled, by an administrator or after failed sign-ins. A disabled account gets nothing else.
notify_disabled_account_owner.label: Notify the owner of a disabled account

offline_mode.description: Stop every call this deployment makes to the internet on its own: the update check, reachability diagnosis, Gravatar, the CRS plugin registry, MaxMind downloads, browser push and agent-built Caddy images. Destinations an administrator configured are still reached.
offline_mode.label: Offline mode

settings.reviewNoConfigChange: These settings do not change the Caddy config.

history.title: Revision history
history.subtitle: Every apply to Caddy, newest first. Compare any two revisions, or restore an earlier one.
history.notRecordedHelp: Applied before revisions kept their values, so it can be neither compared nor restored.
history.same: Pick two different revisions to compare.
history.noChanges: These revisions hold the same settings.
history.configNote: Rendered against today's hosts, so only the settings differ between the two sides.
history.configFailed: The Caddy config could not be rendered for these revisions.
history.notComparable: A revision in this range was applied before values were recorded, so it cannot be compared.
history.restoreHelp: Stages the settings revision #{id} had, on top of anything you already have pending. Review and apply them like any other change.

settings.roleGroupNamesHelp: Name the groups exactly as your provider reports them. Separate several with commas, such as platform-owners, sre-oncall; any one of them grants the role. A role left blank falls back to the prefix above, so the two styles can be mixed. The most privileged match wins.
settings.roleMappingAuthorityHelp: The provider becomes authoritative: a user who loses the admin group is demoted on their next sign-in. The last remaining admin is never demoted.
settings.sharedAgentConfigTitle: Every agent runs the same configuration
settings.stagedSaved: Staged. Review and apply to send it to Caddy.
settings.storedCredentialsHelp: Leave fields blank to keep existing values.
settings.storedSecretHelp: A secret is configured. Its existing value cannot be viewed.
settings.strictTrustedProxiesHelp: Trust the client IP headers only from the configured proxies, and reject spoofed values from untrusted peers.
settings.tailscaleControlServerHelp: Point at a Headscale or other coordination server. Empty uses Tailscale's own.
settings.tailscaleDefaultNodeHelp: The tailnet machine name used by hosts that do not name one of their own. Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.
settings.tailscaleHttp3Help: Lets clients on the tailnet reach served hosts over QUIC. Off by default; the global HTTP/3 setting must also be on.
settings.tailscaleHttp3WarningBody: With HTTP/3 on, Caddy has to reach the control server while it loads a configuration. Whenever the control server is unreachable, that load can hang and lock Caddy's admin API, so no proxy host on this agent can be updated until it comes back.
settings.tailscaleHttp3WarningTitle: HTTP/3 can hang Caddy's config load
settings.tailscaleHelp: Runs a Tailscale node inside Caddy. A proxy host can then be served privately on your tailnet, gated on tailnet identity, or proxied to a backend that only exists on the tailnet.
settings.tailscaleKeyValidationDisabledTitle: Auth keys are not being checked
settings.tailscaleKeyValidationHelp: Catches a revoked, expired or mistyped key here instead of at the next config apply. Needs a Tailscale API access token, because an auth key cannot authenticate to the API.
settings.tailscaleKeyValidationLabel: Check the auth key against the Tailscale API before saving
settings.tailscaleModuleDisabledTitle: The Tailscale module is not enabled
settings.tailscaleStateDirectoryHelp: Where each node keeps its identity, one subdirectory per node. Must be on a volume, or every restart registers a new machine.
settings.trustedProxiesInfoDescription: This fixes client-IP attribution everywhere at once: access logs, analytics, the country map, and any downstream handler using the client_ip placeholder.
settings.trustedProxiesInfoTitle: Nothing else on the host has to change
settings.trustedProxiesScopeDescription: Applied to the main HTTP server
settings.http2Help: Offer HTTP/2 over TLS. HTTP/1.1 is always available, so clients that can't use it still connect
settings.http3Help: Offer HTTP/3 over QUIC on UDP 443. Turn off if a firewall in front of Caddy drops UDP
settings.compressionEnabledHelp: Text, JSON, JavaScript, XML, SVG and fonts are sent with zstd or gzip when the browser accepts it. Images, video and responses the upstream already compressed are left alone. A host can override this in its advanced options
settings.globalCaddyfileHelp: A global options block, site blocks on ports of their own, or both. It can only add: settings CPM manages, like the admin API, storage, certificate automation and ports 80 and 443, are refused by name. Each agent's Caddy checks it before it's saved. A new port also has to be published on the Caddy container.
settings.trustedProxyRangesHelp: CIDRs, IPs, or the private_ranges shorthand, one per line. When CPM runs behind another proxy, Caddy resolves the real client IP from these. Leave empty to keep the current behaviour.

validation.tristate: {label} must be true, false, or left unset

settings.dnsProviderModuleDisabledOption: Its caddy-dns module is disabled in Settings → Caddy build
settings.dnsProvidersSupportedWithUnavailable: {count} providers supported, {unavailable} unavailable because their Caddy module is disabled
settings.tailscaleAuthKeyStored: An auth key is stored. Leave this empty to keep it.
settings.tailscaleAuthKeyHelp: A reusable auth key from the Tailscale admin console. A Caddy placeholder such as '{env.TS_AUTHKEY}' works too, and keeps the key out of the database.
settings.tailscaleTagsHelp: ACL tags applied when a node registers, comma-separated. Most reusable auth keys require at least one, e.g. "tag:caddy".
settings.tailscaleApiTokenStored: A token is stored. Leave this empty to keep it.
settings.tailscaleApiTokenHelp: A tskey-api-… token from the Tailscale admin console. Read access to keys is enough.
settings.tailscaleTailnetHelp: Which tailnet to ask. "-" means the token's own, which is right unless you administer several.
settings.clickhousePasswordStored: A password is stored. Leave this empty to keep it.
settings.clickhousePasswordRequired: Required: the ClickHouse container refuses to start without one.
settings.maxmindLicenceKeyStored: A licence key is stored. Leave this empty to keep it.
settings.oauthProviderRequiredFields: Name, Client ID, and Client secret are required.
settings.localUsersDisabledWithProviders: All accounts are provisioned by the providers below.
settings.localUsersDisabledNoProvider: No provider is enabled, so nobody can sign in.
settings.deleteProviderConfirm: Delete "{name}"? Users who sign in through it lose access.

dnsDelegation.title: Challenge delegation
dnsDelegation.description: Point _acme-challenge at a zone a DNS provider can write, and DNS-01 works for domains whose own DNS has no API. Each name under a delegated domain needs the same CNAME; a wildcard uses its parent's. For a self-hosted BIND server, use the RFC2136 provider instead.
dnsDelegation.empty: No delegations. Every name uses the default provider, or its certificate's.
dnsDelegation.noCnameNeeded: None. This row only picks the provider
dnsDelegation.cnameMissingTitle: Some CNAMEs are missing or point elsewhere
dnsDelegation.cnameMissingDescription: Challenges for those names fail until the record exists. This checks from this server's resolver, which may not see what the certificate authority sees.
dnsDelegation.domainHelp: Covers this name and every name under it. The longest matching domain wins.
dnsDelegation.targetHelp: The name _acme-challenge points to; the challenge record is written there. Leave empty to only choose a provider.
dnsDelegation.providerHelp: Writes the challenge record. Default uses a certificate's own provider, then the default one.
dnsDelegation.rfc2136Hint: There is no manual DNS mode: a record typed by hand would need retyping at every renewal. Delegate to a zone with an API, or to acme-dns below.
dnsDelegation.registerDescription: Creates an account on an acme-dns server for one domain and delegates that domain to it. The account's password is stored encrypted.
dnsDelegation.registerDomainHelp: The domain the account answers for; a wildcard shares its account.
dnsDelegation.serverUrlHelp: HTTPS, unless the server is on a private address or a single-label name such as a Compose service. Your own server is better than a public one.
dnsDelegation.registeredTitle: Registered. Create this record at your DNS host:
dnsDelegation.registeredDescription: Certificates for this domain use the account once the change is applied and the record exists.
dnsDelegation.acmeDnsModuleDisabledDescription: Enable it under Settings → Caddy build and rebuild Caddy before registering.

settings.tailscaleModuleDisabledBody: {reason} These settings still save, but no host is served on the tailnet until the module is compiled in.
settings.tailscaleUserspaceNote: The node runs in userspace inside the Caddy container, so it needs no tailscaled, TUN device or extra published ports. Its identity is kept in the state directory below, so it survives a container recreate.
settings.tailscaleKeyValidationDisabledBody: Nothing here can tell a revoked or expired key from a working one: Caddy finds out only when it tries to register the node, and a node that will not come up makes Caddy reject the entire configuration. Until the key is fixed, no proxy host on any agent can be updated.
settings.faviconCustomSet: A custom favicon is set. Click it to replace it.
settings.faviconNone: No custom favicon, so browsers show their own default. Click the tile to upload one.
settings.updateAvailableBody: You are running {current}. Pull the new images and recreate the stack to move to it.
settings.updateCheckIncomplete: The last check did not complete: {error}
settings.updateUpToDate: {latest} is the newest release published, so this is up to date.
settings.updateNoCheckYet: No check has completed yet. Save or check now to run one.
settings.updateChecksOff: Update checks are off, so nothing is known about newer releases.
settings.updatePrereleaseBody: This install is on stable releases, so the update check won't offer it. To try it, check out the deploy repository's next branch and pull the images. That branch gets every stable release too, so you can go back to main once a stable release catches up.
settings.inferredEnvironmentNote: Saving here stores the value in the database, which takes precedence from then on. The variable can be removed from your .env afterwards.
settings.analyticsInferredNote: Analytics is {state, select, on {on} other {off}} because a ClickHouse password is {password, select, set {set} other {not set}}. Saving makes the choice explicit.
settings.analyticsManagedNote: No COMPOSE_PROFILES entry is needed. The first start pulls the ClickHouse image, which can take several minutes; turning analytics off stops the container and leaves its data volume intact.
settings.analyticsUnmanagedNote: These settings still decide whether analytics runs. Starting ClickHouse itself needs clickhouse in COMPOSE_PROFILES on the host.

httpCache.storageModuleOff: Select its module under Caddy build and rebuild. Until then the cache stays in memory.

badger.description: On disk in the Caddy data volume. Per Caddy, survives a restart.

httpCache.otterSizeHelp: Leave blank for Souin's default of 10,000.
httpCache.redisAddressesHelp: host:port, one per line. Caddy connects to these, so they must be reachable from the Caddy container.
httpCache.redisUsernameHelp: For a Redis ACL user. Leave blank to sign in with the password alone.
httpCache.redisPasswordHelp: Stored encrypted. A wrong one leaves the cache in memory; Caddy's log says why.
httpCache.etcdEndpointsHelp: host:port, one per line, reachable from the Caddy container. Souin cannot pass etcd credentials, so the cluster must not require them.
httpCache.secretStored: Stored. Leave blank to keep it.
httpCache.redisPasswordStored: Stored. Leave blank to keep it, unless you change the servers: then enter it again.
httpCache.cdnProviderHelp: Tags cached responses for the CDN in front of Caddy and purges it when Souin invalidates an entry.

cdnApiKeyHelp.cloudflare: The Global API Key: Souin authenticates with the key and account email, not an API token.
cdnApiKeyHelp.fastly: A Fastly API token allowed to purge this service.

httpCache.cdnEmailHelp: The email of the Cloudflare account the key belongs to.
httpCache.cdnStrategyHelp: A soft purge marks content stale so Fastly can still serve it while it refetches.

captcha.providerHelp: Shown on the sign-in screen's username step. The password step is refused until it is solved, for the form and the API alike. Single sign-on is not affected.
captcha.siteKeyHelp: The public key the provider issued for this site. It is sent to every visitor of the sign-in page.
captcha.secretKeyHelp: Used by this server to check each solve with the provider. Stored encrypted.
captcha.secretKeyStored: A secret key is stored. Leave blank to keep it.
captcha.capInstanceUrlHelp: Where your Cap Standalone server is reached by browsers and by this server, without the site key.
captcha.oidcOnlyBody: There is no username step while local accounts are disabled, so the CAPTCHA only applies once they are enabled again.

hostDefaults.help: What the create dialog starts with, and what a proxy host created through the API gets for a field it leaves out. Hosts that already exist keep their own settings.
hostDefaults.l4Help: What the create dialog starts with, and what an L4 host created through the API gets for a field it leaves out. Hosts that already exist keep their own settings.
hostDefaults.wafFollowsGlobal: Follows the global WAF: on for a new host while it logs or blocks, off while it is off.

rateLimit.help: Zones here apply to every proxy host left to inherit them, and to hosts that merge them with their own. Each host keeps its own count, so a zone of 100 requests a minute allows 100 on every host. The dashboard host never takes them.
rateLimit.enabledHelp: When off, hosts that inherit have no rate limiting. The never-limited list still applies.
rateLimit.allowlistHelp: IP addresses and CIDR ranges no zone ever counts, on any host, one per line, up to {max}. Read after trusted proxies.
rateLimit.unavailable: Rate limiting is not in Caddy

crowdsec.enabledHelp: Every proxy host and L4 host refuses addresses the Local API has a decision against, unless the host opts out in its editor. A ban or captcha decision answers 403, a throttle decision 429 with Retry-After. Decisions are kept in Caddy's memory, so a lookup never waits on the Local API.
crowdsec.moduleDisabledTitle: The CrowdSec module is not in Caddy
crowdsec.moduleDisabledBody: These settings are kept, but nothing is checked until it is: {reason}
crowdsec.apiUrlHelp: Where Caddy reaches your CrowdSec Local API, such as http://crowdsec:8080. Plain http only for a private address, since the bouncer key travels with every request.
crowdsec.apiKeyCreate: Create one on the CrowdSec host:
crowdsec.apiKeyHelp: Stored encrypted and never shown again. A Caddy placeholder such as '{env.CROWDSEC_API_KEY}' works too, and keeps the key out of the database.
crowdsec.apiKeyStored: A bouncer key is stored. Leave blank to keep it.
crowdsec.apiKeyReenter: A bouncer key is stored, but it is only kept while both addresses stay the same. Enter it again.
crowdsec.tickerIntervalHelp: How often Caddy pulls new decisions from the Local API, from 1s to 24h. A new ban takes up to this long to apply.
crowdsec.appsecUrlHelp: Optional. Where Caddy reaches the CrowdSec AppSec component, such as http://crowdsec:7422. Every request is then also sent there for inspection, after rate limiting and geo blocking.
crowdsec.appsecFailOpen: Let requests through when AppSec is unavailable
crowdsec.appsecFailOpenHelp: Off by default: while AppSec cannot be reached or answers with an error, requests are refused.
crowdsec.trustedProxiesTitle: Decisions match the real client address
crowdsec.trustedProxiesBody: The bouncer reads the client IP after Settings > Network > Trusted proxies has been applied. Behind a load balancer or CDN, trust its ranges there, or every request is matched on the proxy's address.
crowdsec.modeHelp: Managed runs CrowdSec in a container beside Caddy, started by the bundled agent and fed Caddy's access log, which stays on and in JSON while it is managed. External uses a CrowdSec you run yourself.
crowdsec.onlineApi: Share signals with CrowdSec's Central API
crowdsec.onlineApiHelp: Off by default. When on, the container registers with CrowdSec, sends it the addresses it decides against and receives the community blocklist in return. When off, nothing leaves this host but the downloads of CrowdSec's detection rules.
crowdsec.managedAppsecHelp: Every request on an HTTP host is also sent to the container's AppSec component, with CrowdSec's virtual patching and generic rules, after rate limiting and geo blocking.
crowdsec.managedRemoteTitle: Only hosts served by the bundled agent are checked
crowdsec.managedRemoteBody: Caddy on another agent's host cannot reach this container, so its hosts are served unchecked in this mode. To cover them, run CrowdSec yourself and choose External.
crowdsec.managedPendingBody: The bundled agent starts the container when these settings are applied. Its first start downloads the image and CrowdSec's detection rules, which takes a few minutes; Caddy serves unchecked until then.
crowdsec.managedNoAgentTitle: No agent is running the container
crowdsec.managedNoAgentBody: The bundled agent is not connected. It starts the container when it reconnects.

email.saveFailed: Failed to save the email settings.
email.incompleteTitle: Email is on, but nothing can be sent yet
email.incompleteBody: Name an SMTP server and a sender address, then save.
email.enabledHelp: Password reset links, user invitations, certificate alerts and notifications go out through this server. When off, the sign-in page offers no password reset.
email.securityHelp: Choose what the server supports. Changing it also changes the port, unless you set a custom one.

securityModes.none: None, for trusted networks only (usually port 25)

email.passwordHelp: Stored encrypted, and never shown again once saved.
email.testHelp: Uses the saved settings. Leave empty to send it to yourself.
email.testNeedsSave: Save a server and a sender address first; the test uses the saved settings.
email.testFailed: The test message could not be sent.
email.testInvalidRecipient: Enter a valid email address to send the test to.
email.alertDaysHelp: Email once a certificate has fewer days than this left. Caddy renews managed certificates well before then, so an alert about one means its renewal is failing. 0 turns alerts off.
email.alertRecipientsHelp: Comma-separated addresses for certificate alerts, which go to every active administrator when this is empty. Notifications go to these too, besides each administrator's own choice under Profile → Notifications.
email.alertsNeedEmailTitle: Alerts and notifications wait for email
email.alertsNeedEmailBody: Certificate alerts wait for the SMTP server above. Notifications go out once it is set up, or to the browsers administrators turn on under Profile → Notifications.
email.alertsNeverChecked: Certificates have not been checked yet. The first check runs a few minutes after the controller starts, then twice a day.
email.notificationsNeverSent: No notification has been sent yet. Events raised within a minute go out together, in one email and one browser notification.
email.notificationsPending: {count, plural, one {# notification is} other {# notifications are}} waiting to be sent.
email.notificationsFailed: The last notification could not be sent: {error}. It is tried again every five minutes, for a day.
email.notificationsNoRecipients: The last notifications were dropped: no recipients are set, and no active administrator has a deliverable address.
email.notificationsPerUser: These turn an event off for everyone. Each administrator chooses their own events, and email or browser, under Profile → Notifications.

unavailable.accessLogOff: Counted from Caddy's access log, in JSON, which is off. Turn it on under Observability → Access logging.
unavailable.accountLockOff: Needs accounts to lock after failed sign-ins, which is off under Authentication → Sign-in.
unavailable.accountDisableOff: Needs accounts to be disabled after repeated failed sign-ins, which is off under Authentication → Sign-in.
unavailable.updateCheckOff: Needs the update check, which is off under General → Updates.
unavailable.geoipOff: The controller downloads GeoIP databases only with GeoIP on and a MaxMind account ID and licence key set, under Geo-blocking → GeoIP databases.

email.testNotificationHelp: Sends one to the recipients above, or every active administrator, straight away.
email.testNotificationNoRecipients: There is no one to send it to: set recipients, or give an active administrator a deliverable address.
email.testNotificationFailed: The test notification could not be sent.

ldap.emptyDescription: Add an LDAP or Active Directory server, and its users sign in on the normal sign-in form with their directory password.
ldap.deleteConfirm: Delete {name}? Its users keep their accounts, but can no longer sign in with their directory password. Those with no other way in also lose their passkeys and are signed out.
ldap.nameHelp: Shown on the sign-in form when there is more than one directory.
ldap.urlHelp: ldaps://host:636, or ldap://host:389 with StartTLS. Only this address is ever dialled.
ldap.startTlsHelp: Upgrade an ldap:// connection to TLS. If the server refuses, the sign-in fails; it never continues unencrypted.
ldap.tlsVerifyHelp: Against the system's certificate authorities and the one below.
ldap.tlsUnverifiedTitle: The server's identity is not checked
ldap.tlsUnverifiedDescription: Anyone who can intercept the connection can read every password typed on the sign-in form. Add the directory's CA certificate below instead.
ldap.caPemHelp: PEM, for a directory whose certificate comes from a private CA. Trusted in addition to the system's.
ldap.modeServiceAccount: A service account finds the user
ldap.modeServiceAccountHelp: A read-only account, or an anonymous search, finds the user's entry and reads their groups; the user's password is then checked with a bind of its own.
ldap.modeUserBindHelp: No service account. The typed username becomes a bind name, and everything else is read with the user's own rights. The recommended Active Directory setup when there is no service account; it needs ldaps:// or StartTLS.
ldap.dnTemplateHelp: Where the typed username replaces '{username}'. A DN such as uid='{username}',ou=people,dc=example,dc=org, escaped; or for Active Directory a UPN such as '{username}'@ad.example.org or a down-level name such as EXAMPLE\'{username}', where a username may hold only letters, digits, dots, hyphens and underscores.
ldap.userBindFilterHelp: Finds the user's own entry after the bind, which must be the account that signed in. The typed username replaces '{username}', escaped.
ldap.bindDnHelp: A read-only service account that searches for users. Leave empty for an anonymous search.
ldap.bindPasswordStoredHelp: Stored. Leave empty to keep it; changing the address or bind DN needs it typed again.
ldap.userFilterHelp: Must match exactly one entry. The typed username replaces '{username}', escaped.
ldap.groupSourceSearch: Search for groups naming the user
ldap.groupFilterHelp: The user's DN replaces '{dn}'. Active Directory's nested form is (member:1.2.840.113556.1.4.1941:='{dn}').
ldap.autoLinkHelp: A first sign-in joins an existing account with the same email address. Only turn this on when the directory's email addresses are set by administrators, not by users: whoever holds an address takes over that account, administrators included.
ldap.groupMappingHelp: Group names are the first part of each group's DN, such as Proxy Admins for CN=Proxy Admins,OU=Groups,DC=example,DC=org. Nested groups count with Active Directory's group filter.

test.title: Test the connection
test.help: Checks the settings above without saving them. With a username and password it also signs in as that user and shows what the directory returns.
test.connected: Connected, and the service account can read the base DN.
test.connectedUserBind: Connected, and TLS is working. Binding as the user can check nothing more without a user: add a test username and password to try a sign-in.
test.signedIn: Connected, and the test user signed in.

stage.connect: Could not connect to the directory, or the TLS handshake failed.
stage.bind: The directory refused the bind DN and password.
stage.search: The service account cannot read the base DN.

signIn.invalidInput: Enter a test username and password.
signIn.invalidCredentials: The directory refused the test user's password.
signIn.notFound: No entry matches the test username.
signIn.ambiguous: More than one entry matches the test username. Narrow the user filter.
signIn.refusedUsername: A UPN or down-level bind name takes only letters, digits, dots, hyphens and underscores in the username.
signIn.otherEntry: The test user's password was accepted, but the user filter found a different entry. Narrow the user filter to the user's own account.
signIn.unavailable: The sign-in failed partway. The server log says where.

modeHelp.off: Anyone may turn on an authenticator app or add a passkey from their Profile, but nobody has to.
modeHelp.admins: Administrators who sign in with a password need an authenticator app or a passkey. Single sign-on accounts are left to their identity provider.
modeHelp.all: Everyone who signs in with a password needs an authenticator app or a passkey. Single sign-on accounts are left to their identity provider.

mfaPolicy.graceDaysHelp: How long an account has once the policy reaches it. Until then a banner asks for setup; afterwards setup comes before anything else at sign-in. 0 asks at once.
mfaPolicy.breakGlass: Locked out by the policy? Run cpm-server --lift-mfa-policy inside the web container to turn it off.

saml.spEntityIdHelp: What the identity provider knows CPM as, and the audience every assertion must name. Left blank, it is the metadata URL below.
saml.linkDomainsHelp: Comma-separated. A first sign-in whose email is in one of these domains joins the CPM account with the same email; any other needs an account of its own.
saml.groupsAttributeHelp: The assertion attribute listing the user's groups, one value per group.
